summary: Over-the-top eggplant parmigiana: peeled eggplant planks salted and drained at least 30 minutes, breaded with flour, egg and panko, fried until fork-tender, layered three times with San Marzano tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, Parmesan and basil, baked 20 minutes at 400°F and topped with fresh heirloom tomatoes; serves 6.
glance: 3 large or 5 smaller globe, about 4 pounds, drained with salt at least 30 minutes
400°F for about 20 minutes, just to melt the cheese
faq: Why salt and drain the eggplant?

The author doesn't for most uses, but it's worthwhile here: extracting some liquid makes the eggplant fry up firm yet fork-tender, with no mush factor. Layer with kosher salt in a colander, weight with a plate and cans, and drain at least 30 minutes.
What's the tip for breading?

Use one hand to put the eggplant in the flour, egg and breadcrumbs, and the other to toss it in the breadcrumbs and into the skillet: one hand for the wet stuff and the other for the dry, so you avoid getting your hands breaded.
Which canned tomatoes are best?
The finest canned tomatoes for Italian dishes come from San Marzano; look for that name on the can. Simmer the sauce with garlic 15 minutes without salt, because the eggplant retains residual salt.
Does the eggplant cook in the oven?
No: it should be tender to a fork after frying because oven baking is just to melt the cheese.
What do I serve with it?
Just a green salad makes a celebratory dinner; top each stack with a toss of heirloom tomatoes and basil.

summary: Congee with crispy yuba: Chinese-style rice simmered 1 1/4 to 1 1/2 hours in 9 cups of water into a creamy porridge, topped with pan-fried yuba (tofu skin), crispy shallot rings, quick-pickled red cabbage, cilantro, sesame oil and flaky salt; vegan, serves 4, 15 minutes active.
glance: 3/4 cup rice, 9 cups water, 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, stirring every 10 minutes
faq: What is congee?

Rice cooked in copious amounts of water until it falls apart into porridge. Wherever rice is a staple, from China to India, some form of congee is beloved; it is often a breakfast dish and considered a recuperative, restorative meal.
What toppings should congee have?

It's a blank palette, but it's usually best to include something crunchy, something green, something salty and a small but substantial hit of protein. Other options: sliced hard-boiled egg, toasted crushed peanuts, green onions, kimchi, tofu, pickled ginger.
How do I make crispy yuba?

Break up the yuba and cover with boiling water for 5 minutes, drain, rinse and pat dry, then close to serving time pat dry again and fry in hot oil (in two batches if needed) until golden brown; it browns quickly and sticks together somewhat like an egg. Sprinkle with salt.
Can I make thicker congee?
Yes: use less water and shorter cooking times for a thicker, less broken down congee. This approach is more common in Japan, where the porridge is called okayu.
How do I make the shallots crispy?
Fry sliced shallot rings in a single layer in hot oil, tossing once or twice, until dark golden brown, then drain on paper towels and salt.

summary: Brussels sprout and apple hash from the Herbivoracious cookbook: onion and diced apple browned in butter, then sliced sprouts cooked about 10 minutes with sage and rosemary until well browned, finished with champagne vinegar and honey; gluten-free, serves 3 to 4 in 20 minutes.
glance: 1 pound, sliced about 1/4 inch thick, cooked about 10 minutes until wilted and well browned
1 crisp apple such as Pink Lady, peeled, cored, finely diced
faq: What do I serve it with?

The author thinks of it as a side that goes well with mac & cheese or a rustic soup and salad, but he's fried up a plate just for himself with a slice of toasted artisanal wheat bread and called it dinner.
How do I get the sprouts nicely browned?
Cook them, stirring occasionally, with a big pinch of salt, sage and rosemary until wilted and well browned, about 10 minutes, then toss with the vinegar and honey, scraping the browned bits.
Can I change it?
Add toasted pecans, hazelnuts or dried cherries; swap the champagne vinegar for apple cider vinegar, sherry vinegar or orange juice; or replace the apple with a crisp pear.
How do I adjust the seasoning?
It will likely need more salt, and you may want more honey or vinegar to suit your taste.
Where is it from?
The author demoed it on KCTS from his cookbook, and a reader pointed out the recipe wasn't on the site.

summary: Pozole rojo de frijol in 40 minutes: onion and garlic sauteed, simmered with tomatoes, oregano, canned pinto beans and hominy for ten minutes, then finished with pureed soaked dried red chiles and lime juice for a mildly spicy, sour broth; serves 4 as a one-pot meal or 8 as a first course.
glance: 4 as a one-pot meal or 8 as a first course
10 minutes after adding the beans and hominy
1 or 2 dried de arbol, ancho or guajillo, soaked 20 minutes and pureed
Gluten-free; vegan option (skip the cheese-free garnishes check)
yield: 4 as a one-pot meal or 8 as a first course
faq: What is pozole?

A soup or thin stew made all over Mexico, dating back to pre-Columbian times. Vegetarian pozole is almost a non-sequitur because the original is heavy on the pig, but this version is delicious and filling.
What makes it pozole rojo?
As long as it has hominy and some kind of red chile in it, you are in the ballpark; there are more variations than you can count. Pozole verde includes ground pumpkin seeds.
Can I use dried hominy and beans?

Yes, for a more leisurely and even better soup: hominy corn is available dried, soaked overnight and boiled for several hours, very much like dried beans. The canned versions make it a weeknight supper.
How do I adjust the heat and sourness?

Add half of the pureed chiles and all the lime juice, taste, and add salt and more lime juice or tomatoes for a piquant broth; add more of the chile paste to reach your preferred heat level and pass the rest as a condiment.
What garnishes go with pozole?
Avocado slices, cilantro, lime wedges, tortilla chips, shredded cabbage or lettuce, onions and radishes, on a big platter so diners choose for themselves; much of the fun is in the accompaniments.

summary: Insalata caprese with Purple Cherokee heirloom tomatoes: ripe tomato slices topped with fresh (buffalo) mozzarella, generous fruity extra-virgin olive oil, flaky sea salt and basil, with only 5 ingredients that go together in 3 minutes; serves 4.
glance: 2 large ripe heirloom tomatoes, 2-3 balls fresh mozzarella, olive oil, flaky sea salt, basil
faq: What makes great caprese?

With only 5 ingredients and no cooking, the greatness is completely determined by their quality: the finest, ripest heirloom tomatoes, sweet and milky fresh mozzarella, superb olive oil, flaky sea salt and fragrant basil.
How do I slice the tomatoes and cheese?
Core the tomatoes and slice about 1/4 to 3/8 inch thick; slice the mozzarella (preferably buffalo) a little thinner. Optionally add a handful of heirloom cherry tomatoes.
How do I assemble it?

Arrange all of the tomatoes in a single layer on a platter, top each slice with a piece of cheese, drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle on the salt and finish with basil chiffonade or torn leaves.
When is the best time to make it?
During the brief period when tomatoes are good enough to eat it several times a week; the author used Purple Cherokees and mixed heirloom cherry tomatoes.
Which salt should I use?
Flaky sea salt; Maldon is ideal.

summary: Middle Eastern panzanella: well-toasted pita, ripe tomatoes and cucumber tossed just before serving with red onion, cilantro, mint, olive oil, lemon juice and salt and garnished with sumac, similar to Lebanese fattoush; vegan, 15 minutes, serves 1 as an entree or 4 as a small side.
glance: 1 as an entree or 4 as a small side dish
yield: 1 as an entree or 4 as a small side dish
faq: What is panzanella?

The classic Italian salad of slightly stale rustic bread soaking up the juices of spectacular ripe summer tomatoes, a great basis for improvisation. This version uses crispy toasted pita, mint, cilantro and sumac for a Middle Eastern spin, similar to Lebanese fattoush.
What is sumac?

A lovely, deep purple spice with a tangy taste used throughout the Middle East as a final garnish on everything from hummus to kebabs, as much for color as flavor. If you can't find it, the salad is still delicious.
When do I toss the salad?
Just before serving, so the pita doesn't get soggy: cut the pita, tomatoes and cucumber into bite-sized pieces and toss with the onion, herbs, olive oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
What can I add?
Other fresh herbs, black olives, a handful of chickpeas, feta cheese, or a dollop of thick yogurt.
Do I need to peel the cucumber?
Only if the peel is tough.

summary: Chocolate-chunk bread pudding: cubed challah or brioche tossed gently with a custard of 4 eggs and 2 cups of milk (the reliable 2 eggs to 1 cup milk ratio) and chunks of 70% bittersweet chocolate, baked covered at 350°F for about 1 hour 15 minutes until 185°F inside; serves 6-8.
glance: 350°F, covered with foil, until 185°F in the center (about 1 hour 15 minutes)
14 ounces slightly stale challah or brioche, most of the crust removed, 3/4-inch cubes
faq: What is the key to bread pudding?
It's a custard, albeit heavily garnished with bread. Treat it appropriately in ratios and temperatures and you have a lot of freedom to tweak the components and be assured of a great dessert.
What is the custard ratio?
2 large eggs to 1 cup of milk, a reliable ratio for a free-standing custard like flan, from Michael Ruhlman's Ratio; it works fine for bread pudding too.
Why bake it covered?
To avoid overcooking the edges, the author bakes it in one large dish covered in a relatively slow oven. Individual ramekins would also work, even in a water bath like flan or creme brulee.
How do I know it's done?
An internal temperature in the center of 185°F, or by testing with a fork and a bite: well set, but not overcooked and rubbery. Rest ten minutes.
How big should the chocolate pieces be?
Not a whole mouthful but a lot bigger than a chocolate chip, so they stay molten. Serve with whipped cream, heavy cream or vanilla ice cream, optionally with a bit of bourbon whisked into the cream.

summary: Stuffed and baked polenta: a layer of polenta topped with sauteed mushrooms and kale in tarragon bechamel and a second polenta layer, covered with asiago and Parmesan and baked at 400°F about 30 minutes in a 9x13 pan; can be assembled a day ahead; serves 8, 45 minutes active.
glance: 9 cups cooked (3 cups raw); quick-cooking works
2 pounds button mushrooms, 1 bunch kale, 2 cups tarragon bechamel
400°F for about 30 minutes, until hot through and golden brown
faq: Why a baked dish?

The author loves baked dishes for entertaining or when busy with kids because they mind their own business in the oven. This one has just enough cheese to seem rich without blowing the week's calorie budget.
What polenta should I use?
Quick-cooking polenta works fine; the author likes the de la Estancia brand from Argentina for its pronounced corn flavor, but you can use any polenta.
Can I make it ahead?
Yes: prepare and bake immediately or refrigerate and bake the next day, allowing more time in the oven if refrigerated.
How do I cook the filling?
Saute onion and garlic, add salt, chile flakes and sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and the bottom of the pan seems dry, then add the kale until wilted and tender, and the lemon zest.
How do I assemble it?

Grease a 9x13 pan at least 2 inches deep, spread half of the polenta (squish it into place if it has cooled and solidified), top with the mushroom mixture, then the tarragon bechamel and the remaining polenta, and scatter the grated cheeses on top.

summary: The SuperFrico: a grilled cheese sandwich with a built-in cheese crisp. Make a cheddar-and-provolone sandwich in a buttered cast-iron skillet, then melt mixed Cheddar and Parmigiano in the hot pan until the fat cooks out and it starts to crisp, press the sandwich on top to weld the frico on, and cook one more minute; makes one sandwich.
glance: 1/2 cup grated aged provolone or oak-smoked cheddar
3 tablespoons cheddar mixed with 2 teaspoons grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
cast iron, medium heat, press with a smaller skillet
faq: What is a SuperFrico?

A grilled cheese sandwich with a built-in cheese crisp: the author reasoned that the best bits of grilled cheese, lasagna, gratin or mac and cheese are where the cheese gets brown and crispy, so he made a frico (cheese crisp) in the skillet and welded it to the sandwich.
How do I make it?

Grill the basic sandwich until golden on both sides, remove it, lower the heat to medium and sprinkle the cheese mix in the still-hot skillet in a shape slightly larger than the sandwich. When the fat begins to cook out and the cheese browns, put the sandwich back on top, press down, cook one more minute, then flip with a thin spatula.
What if there are leftover crispy bits?
Retrieve any more crispy bits from the skillet and place them on top of the sandwich.
Is the cheese vegetarian?
The author notes folks often ask how to know whether cheese uses animal, vegetable or microbial rennet; the best way to find out is to ask the manufacturer.
What bread and cheese did he use?

Artisan sourdough (a Tall Grass bakery loaf is a favorite), aged provolone or oak-smoked cheddar inside, and Beecher's Flagship Cheddar with Parmigiano for the frico. It was entered in the 2010 Seattle Cheese Festival grilled cheese contest.

summary: Jamaican rice and peas: basmati rice cooked in coconut milk with kidney beans, garlic, crushed scallions, thyme and an optional whole Scotch bonnet, made in a rice cooker or on the stovetop in 10 minutes active (40 total); vegan, serves 4.
glance: one 14-ounce can coconut milk plus water (stovetop: 2 3/4 cups water for 2 cups rice)
1 1/2 cups cooked kidney or other beans
faq: What is Jamaican rice and peas?

A classic Jamaican dish traditionally served on Sundays; the "peas" are actually kidney beans, pigeon peas or cowpeas. The rice is richly flavored with coconut milk, garlic, crushed scallions, thyme and, if you dare, a Scotch bonnet or habanero pepper.
How hot will it be?
Even though the pepper is left whole, it will infuse a subtle bit of heat. For more, cut a slit in the pepper, or, if you're really crazy, cut it up while wearing rubber gloves.
How do I make it in a rice cooker or on the stovetop?

Rice cooker: 3 measures of rice, the coconut milk, water to the 3-cup line plus 1/4 cup, plus the other ingredients, on a normal cycle. Stovetop: 2 cups rice, the can of coconut milk and 2 3/4 cups water in a pot with a tight lid, boil, cover and bare simmer until the water is absorbed.
Can I use cooking liquid from the beans?
If you make the beans from scratch, substitute 1 cup of the bean liquid for part of the water for a "dirty rice" look with a slightly earthier flavor.
How do I serve it?
Remove the whole green onions, thyme sprigs and chile, fluff the rice and garnish with sliced green onion. It goes well with dhal puri roti.
